scale_007:n1.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the initial setup of our identity provider tenant ({{vendor}}) as the foundation for company-wide SSO, role-based access, MFA, and provisioning. This is a security-foundational action, so you must prepare everything but not finalize or activate any settings — a human must review and approve before go-live.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already known: our company name, primary domain, the {{vendor}} tenant/org name we want to use, an admin contact email, and any naming conventions for groups/roles we prefer.

Then, using your configured credentials, do as much of the following as the {{vendor}} admin console/tools allow: create or configure the {{vendor}} organization/tenant, set the org display name, configure the primary domain association, and set up initial security defaults (e.g., MFA policy draft, session timeout draft, password policy draft) in an unpublished/draft state where possible. Draft a proposed role/group structure (e.g., Admin, IT, Employee) and a provisioning approach outline, without applying it live.

Produce a clear checklist summarizing: tenant name, domain, draft MFA policy, draft role/group structure, and any settings that still require manual verification in the console (e.g., domain ownership confirmation, final MFA enforcement, admin role assignments).

Do not activate MFA enforcement, do not finalize domain trust, and do not approve or submit any changes that affect production access. Once your checklist and drafts are ready, stop for human sign-off. Report back with: a summary of what was configured or drafted, any values you need me to confirm, and the exact remaining steps that require my manual approval in the {{vendor}} console.

scale_007:n2.prompt:
You are helping me define role-based access groups in {{vendor}}, our SSO/identity provider, as part of setting up SSO and access management. Approval is required before any changes take effect — a human must explicitly approve before changes are applied.

Please do the following:
1. Ask me for: (a) our {{vendor}} domain/tenant, (b) the list of company tools/apps we need to control access to, (c) our organizational structure (departments, teams, seniority levels) or an existing roster if I have one, and (d) any known compliance or least-privilege requirements.
2. Using this info, draft a proposed set of role-based groups (e.g., by department, function, and seniority) with clear naming conventions, intended membership rules (dynamic where possible, based on attributes like department or title), and which apps/tools each group should be assigned to.
3. Where {{vendor}} supports it, prepare the configuration as code (e.g., a Terraform-style definition or equivalent declarative config) covering groups, membership rules, and app assignments, so it's reviewable before being applied. Also prepare the equivalent manual steps via the dashboard or REST API in case code-managed config isn't used.
4. Summarize the proposed groups, their membership logic, and app assignments in a clear document or table for my review.
5. Do not create, modify, or apply any groups, rules, or app assignments in {{vendor}} yet. Use your configured credentials only to read existing configuration if needed for context (e.g., current users, apps, or groups) — never to create or change anything at this stage.

Done looks like: a complete, reviewed draft of role-based groups, membership rules, and app assignments, plus prepared code/config artifacts, ready for my inspection. Report back with the full proposal, any assumptions you made, and then stop for human sign-off before applying anything.

scale_007:n3.prompt:
You are helping me configure SSO for each of our company applications in {{vendor}}, our identity provider, as part of setting up company-wide SSO and access management. Approval is required before any change goes live, so you must prepare everything but stop before applying changes.

First, ask me for: (1) the list of applications we need to connect (note which are pre-built catalog integrations vs. custom SAML/OIDC/header-based apps), (2) my {{vendor}} org/tenant details, and (3) any role/group structure I want mapped to app assignments.

Then, for each app:
- Check whether {{vendor}}'s catalog has a pre-built integration; if so, prepare the configuration (attributes, sign-on mode, assignment groups) using the dashboard or {{vendor}}'s documented REST APIs, using your configured credentials.
- For apps not in the catalog, draft the custom SAML/OIDC/header-based configuration following {{vendor}}'s documented walkthroughs, noting required metadata (entity ID, ACS URL, certificates, claims).
- Where possible, express the app, group, and policy configuration as code (e.g., via {{vendor}}'s Terraform provider or equivalent) so it's reviewable and reproducible rather than only clicked through in the UI.
- Compile a per-app checklist showing: app name, integration type (catalog/custom), configuration status (drafted/ready), assigned groups/roles, and any open questions or missing metadata from the app vendor.

Do not activate, publish, or push any configuration changes to production — only prepare drafts, config-as-code files, and documentation.

When done, report back: the full list of apps with their configuration status, links to any draft code/config files, a summary of custom integrations requiring extra input from app owners, and a clear note that this is ready and must stop for human sign-off before applying.

scale_007:n4.prompt:
You are helping me enable MFA policies in {{vendor}}, our SSO/identity provider, as part of setting up SSO & access management. Please use your configured credentials to access our {{vendor}} admin console/API.

First, ask me for anything you need that's missing: our {{vendor}} tenant/org details, the list of company apps and groups needing policies, which apps are considered sensitive (requiring stronger auth like FIDO2 security keys or passkeys), and our baseline device posture requirements (managed, encrypted, screen-locked).

Then draft a complete MFA policy proposal covering:
1. Context-aware conditional access rules per app/group (network, device, location, risk signals).
2. Device posture checks required before granting app sessions.
3. Passwordless sign-in options (passkeys, authenticator, platform biometrics) documented for employees.
4. A rule requiring FIDO2 security keys or passkeys specifically for sensitive apps.
5. Fallback/enrollment factors for standard apps (e.g., push, authenticator).

Prepare the policy configuration as a clear, reviewable document (or staged/draft policy in {{vendor}} if the platform supports a non-live draft state) — do not activate or apply any policy that would affect live user access. Include a summary table mapping app/group → policy tier → required factors → device posture rules.

Because approval is required before changes go live, do not enable, publish, or enforce any policy yourself. Prepare everything and then stop for human sign-off.

Report back with: the draft policy document/summary table, links or references to the draft configuration in {{vendor}} if created, any open questions (e.g., ambiguous app sensitivity classifications), and a short list of next steps for me to review and approve before activation.

scale_007:n5.prompt:
You are helping me provision our existing employees into {{vendor}} as part of rolling out SSO and access management. The goal is for every current team member to have a correct user profile in {{vendor}}, assigned to the right groups and roles, without creating duplicates or granting the wrong access.

Ask me for anything missing before you start:
- My company's primary email domain
- The source of truth for current staff: an export from our HR system, a spreadsheet, or a live HRIS integration if one is already connected to {{vendor}}
- The role or group mapping we agreed on, such as department or title mapped to {{vendor}} groups
- Any accounts to exclude, such as contractors, service accounts, or people who have left

Use your configured credentials to connect to {{vendor}}'s directory API or admin console. Then:
1. List the users already in {{vendor}}. Handle pagination so none are missed.
2. Compare that list with the source-of-truth roster by email. Group everyone into three buckets: to create, already present (update if any profile fields differ), and in {{vendor}} but not on the roster (flag only, never delete).
3. For each user to create, prepare the profile: first name, last name, work email, department, title, manager if available, and the groups they will join under the role mapping. Make sure MFA enrollment will be required at first sign-in.
4. Present the full change plan to me as a table. Show each user, the action, the field changes, and the group assignments. Then stop for human sign-off. Do not create, update, or assign anything until I explicitly approve.
5. After I approve, apply the changes. Use bulk or SCIM/HRIS-driven provisioning if {{vendor}} supports it for our setup.

Done looks like this: every approved user exists in {{vendor}} with the correct groups, and no unapproved changes were made. Report back with counts of users created, updated, and flagged, plus any failures and their error messages. Also list any users whose role mapping was unclear.

scale_007:n6.prompt:
You are helping me test that Single Sign-On (via Okta or Google Workspace SSO, whichever we've configured) is working correctly across every company tool we've integrated. If you don't already have this information, ask me for: (1) the identity provider we're using (Okta or Google Workspace), (2) the list of company apps/tools that have been connected for SSO (e.g. Slack, Google Drive, Zoom, GitHub, Salesforce, etc.), and (3) which of these apps require MFA and what role-based access groups exist for each.

Once you have this, using my configured credentials, go through each connected app one by one and perform a login regression test:
- Navigate to each app's login page and initiate login via SSO (not username/password).
- Confirm the identity provider login screen appears and authentication completes successfully.
- Confirm MFA is triggered where it's supposed to be required.
- Confirm the logged-in user lands with the correct role/permissions level based on their assigned access group (spot-check at least one test account per role tier if multiple exist).
- Note any app where SSO fails, MFA doesn't trigger, redirect loops occur, or the user lands with incorrect permissions.

Produce a simple test report as a table: App Name | SSO Login Success (Y/N) | MFA Triggered (Y/N) | Correct Role/Access (Y/N) | Notes/Errors.

Done looks like: every app on the list has been tested and the report is complete, with any failures clearly flagged and described so I can route them to the right owner for fixing. This testing itself is fully drivable by you — just log in through each SSO flow and record results plainly. Report back with the full table and a short summary of which apps passed cleanly and which need follow-up.

scale_007:n7.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the team-wide rollout of SSO enforcement (Okta or Google Workspace SSO, whichever we use) across our company tools. This is an async step: some results (employee migration status) will only be visible over the following days, so plan for polling/verification rather than a one-shot completion.

Please do the following:
1. Ask me for: which identity provider we use (Okta or Google SSO), the list of connected apps/tools requiring SSO, the target rollout groups/roles, the MFA policy requirements, and the rollout timeline/phases (e.g., pilot group first, then org-wide).
2. Draft a phased rollout plan: which user groups get SSO+MFA enforcement in which order, with suggested dates.
3. Draft the internal communication (email/Slack message) explaining the change, why it matters, what employees need to do (e.g., enroll MFA, use new login flow), and support/escalation contact.
4. Prepare a checklist of per-group enforcement toggles to be applied in the admin console (list exact group names and the policy setting each needs), but do NOT toggle or apply any enforcement policy yourself.
5. Prepare a monitoring plan: what to check afterward (login success rates, MFA enrollment %, help-desk tickets) and how often to poll status.
6. Compile all drafts (plan, communication, checklist, monitoring plan) into a single summary document for my review.

Do not apply any enforcement changes, do not send communications, and do not toggle policies in the admin console — a human must explicitly approve and apply these changes. Once your drafts are ready, present them to me and then stop for human sign-off.

Report back with: the finalized rollout plan, draft communications, the enforcement checklist, and the monitoring plan, clearly labeled as pending my approval.
